🇮🇷🇮🇶 Iran and Iraq commit to fully implementing their security agreement

Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Iraq's National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi in Tehran on Saturday. Al-Aboudi was leading a high-level Iraqi security delegation.

Rezaei called for the security agreement between the two countries to be fully implemented and for security on their shared border. He said an independent, strong and developed Iraq could be one of the pillars of a new security order in West Asia, and that foreign powers must not be allowed to undermine economic cooperation between Tehran and Baghdad.

Al-Aboudi said Iraq is committed to implementing the agreement in full and will not allow its airspace or territory to be used against Iran or any of its other neighbors.

⚡️ Enemy lacks capability for ground war against Iran: Army commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The deputy commander of the Army’s ground forces says that Iran’s enemies lack the capability to engage in a ground war against the Iranian Armed Forces, warning that any such move would be met with a decisive response.

Brigadier General Nozar Nemati said on Saturday that the Iranian ground forces had been deployed along the borders before the outbreak of the war and had made the necessary preparations to defend the country’s land frontiers.
​
“The enemy is aware of the capabilities of the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Armed Forces on the ground and knows that any action would be met with a decisive response,” Nemati told reporters.
​
He said the Army’s ground forces had fully carried out their assigned missions alongside other branches of the Armed Forces during the 12-day war and subsequent military developments.
​
Nemati added that the Army’s missile and drone units had been actively involved in military operations since the beginning of the 12-day war and continued to carry out their missions.
​
Asked about the possibility of enemy ground forces entering the war, Nemati said Iran’s adversaries understood the risks of such an escalation.
​
“The enemy knows better than anyone that it does not have the capability to enter a ground war with the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he said, adding that any such move would provoke a response from Iranian forces.
​
Nemati also said Iran shared borders with 14 countries and maintained security along its frontiers despite instability in some neighboring states.
​
He said border guards, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), the Army’s ground forces and other military units shared responsibility for protecting the country’s borders.
